test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 15 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In which year was the first-ever motion to remove a Supreme Court Justice signed by the members of Parliament?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1991**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first-ever motion to remove a Supreme Court Justice in India was signed in **1991**.
 
• The motion was targeted at Justice V. Ramaswami, who faced allegations of financial irregularities.
 
• The motion was initiated by the then Law Minister Subramanian Swamy.
 
• The process led to the formation of a three-member judicial committee to investigate the charges.
 
• Although the committee found him guilty, the motion did not pass in the Lok Sabha due to lack of requisite majority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Impeachment Process of Judges**

 
 
• The procedure for the removal of judges is outlined in Article 124(4) and Article 217 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• A judge can be removed on grounds of proven misbehavior or incapacity.
 
• The process can be initiated in either House of Parliament.
 
• The motion needs to be supported by a specified number of members before it can be admitted.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Committee**
 
 
• Once the motion is admitted, a three-member committee investigates the charges.
 
• The committee consists of a Supreme Court judge, a Chief Justice of a High Court, and a distinguished jurist.
 
 
 
• **Final Decision**
 
 
• If the committee finds the judge guilty, the House can take up the motion for debate and voting.
 
• The motion must be passed by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting in each House of Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**
 
 
• Justice V. Ramaswami was the first Supreme Court judge to face an impeachment motion.
 
• The case highlighted the need for transparency and accountability in the judiciary.
